title: The CDC suggests letting a 15-month-old find you behind a chair
summary: The CDC's 15-month page suggests letting the child watch you go behind a chair, then waiting for the child to come find you.
body: Among activities at 15 months, the CDC describes a simple game: let the child watch you go behind a chair, then wait for the child to come find you. The page offers this as play, not as a milestone most children already pass. It is a US activity idea about a person who has gone out of view.

sources.title: Milestones by 15 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the activity of going behind a chair and waiting for the child to find you. Paraphrased without the page's game title so it stays one claim.
